title: Google Quietly Cuts Free Storage to 5GB for New Accounts Without Phone Verification

body:
Google has reduced the default free storage for new accounts from 15GB to just 5GB, requiring users to verify a phone number to unlock the full allocation. The change, first spotted by 9to5Google through updated support pages, has been rolling out since March 2026 and appears to target regions including Kenya and Nigeria, though reports suggest broader enforcement is underway.

The move is designed to combat abuse of Google's storage system, where users would create multiple accounts to pool free storage. Under the new policy, accounts created without a linked phone number receive 5GB shared across Gmail, Google Drive, and Google Photos — a third of the previous allocation. Linking a phone number restores the familiar 15GB tier.

Google has framed this as a security measure rather than a cost-cutting exercise, though the timing aligns with the company's broader push toward paid Google One plans that bundle AI features like Gemini alongside expanded storage. The cheapest Google One tier starts at $1.99 per month for 100GB.

For Indian-Americans, the change carries particular weight. India is one of Google's largest markets by user count, and many NRI families manage multiple accounts for relatives back home — often created without phone verification. Students on F-1 visas who use university Google Workspace accounts may also find their personal backup options constrained if they create secondary accounts without Indian or US phone numbers.

The broader context is a quiet tightening across Big Tech's free tiers. Apple's iCloud still offers 5GB free, while Microsoft provides 5GB with OneDrive. Google's 15GB had long been the most generous default — and for many users, it still will be, provided they hand over a phone number.
author: Diaspora Desk
